data.body:
RE-REVIEW AFTER THE AC8 CORRECTION: PASS, 0 blocking, 3 advisory. Certified at b794da8fc1.

The top advisory is one I CAUSED and am deliberately not fixing; recording the reasoning rather than silently skipping it. It says the Scope section lists exactly two touched files while my corrected AC8 now names a third (tests/unit/test_rebar_debug_step7_class_review.py), so Scope and AC8 contradict each other. That is accurate. Its stated failure scenario is 'an implementer follows Scope, edits only the two docs, and ships without the required test - then AC8 and AC9 fail at close.'

That scenario cannot occur here: the work is already implemented, merged as Gerrit 2076 (commit 9296241726), and the test EXISTS and passes. The coherence gap is real but has no remaining consequence, and closing it would cost another full review cycle on a ticket that is otherwise ready to close. If this plan were still unimplemented I would fix it; as a post-merge record it is not worth the pass. Anyone editing this ticket later should add the test file to Scope.

The other two advisories: P6 ac-quality (3 criteria bundle deliverables with 'and') and an E6/E1 note that neither Approach nor Testing describes authoring the test - the same Scope/AC8 gap seen from the other side. Both are the same post-hoc situation and are recorded here rather than actioned.
